fixes.explanation: It's true, friend. The man says, "Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”" (Luke 12:19) He fully plans to say it. The speech is all in his head, and God hasn't weighed in yet.

That's the one, baker. The man says, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me." (Luke 12:13) He asks Jesus to step in on an inheritance. Notice he's someone in the crowd, and he asks Jesus straight out.

I can see the guess, but this one isn't a loan. Nothing in the text says the brother borrowed a thing. The man asks Jesus to tell his brother "…to divide the inheritance with me." (Luke 12:13) It's about an inheritance, not a debt.

The man's request does involve his brother and an inheritance, so I get the guess. But Jesus never says money always does that. His reason is, "…one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions." (Luke 12:15)

That would be a very different story, friend. But the plan the man gives isn't about giving anything away. He says, "I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods." (Luke 12:18) That's the plan in his own words.
